classification.difficultyReason: Follow the prescribed ray directions, measure the three sectors and add the measurements to check the explicitly supplied revolution rule.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Place $O$ in the centre of your page. Allow at least 10 cm of space around $O$.

answer.short: Point $O$ centred on the page, with at least 10 cm of space around it.
answer.worked: Place and label $O$ centrally, leaving at least 10 cm above, below and to either side for the construction.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw two rays, $OA$ and $OB$, going off to the right; one upwards, one downwards.

answer.short: Sample construction: $OA$ goes upwards to the right and $OB$ goes downwards to the right.
answer.worked: On the construction from part a, draw $OA$ at $60^{\circ}$ above the horizontal to the right and $OB$ at $60^{\circ}$ below it. These are sample directions; other suitable directions are valid.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw a third ray, $OC$, going to the left.

answer.short: Sample construction: draw $OC$ horizontally to the left from $O$.
answer.worked: Add $OC$ horizontally to the left to the same construction. The three rays divide the revolution at $O$ into three adjacent angles.

spec.description: Authored sample construction, reduced for the answer edition; the source supplies instructions rather than a diagram.
spec.mathematics: OA has direction 60 degrees, OB has direction 300 degrees and OC has direction 180 degrees. The three intervening sectors are each 120 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no sample rays or measurements appear in the student prompt.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Measure the sizes of $\angle AOB$, $\angle BOC$ and $\angle COA$.

answer.short: Answers depend on the construction. For the sample: $\angle AOB=120^{\circ}$, $\angle BOC=120^{\circ}$ and $\angle COA=120^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Centre the protractor at $O$, align its baseline with an arm and read the appropriate scale for each adjacent sector. For the sample construction:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOB&=120^{\circ}\\\angle BOC&=120^{\circ}\\\angle COA&=120^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Check that they obey the statement, ‘Angles in a revolution add to $360^{\circ}$’.

answer.short: The three measured angles total approximately $360^{\circ}$. For the sample, $120^{\circ}+120^{\circ}+120^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Add the three measurements. For the sample:
$$\angle AOB+\angle BOC+\angle COA=120^{\circ}+120^{\circ}+120^{\circ}=360^{\circ}.$$
The angles form one revolution at $O$. Small differences in measured totals can arise from drawing or measurement error.
